p.src: Now the blacksmiths in the courtyard, exhausted by several days of hard work, had all fallen asleep that night. When they rose at daybreak to resume their forging, they found that the three weapons had vanished from beneath the awning. Stunned and alarmed, they searched everywhere. Just then the three young princes came out of the palace to inspect the work. The blacksmiths all kowtowed and said, “Young lords, no one knows where the divine masters’ three weapons have gone.”

p.src: The young princes trembled with fright on hearing this. “Perhaps our masters put them away during the night,” they said. They hurried to the Baosha Pavilion and, seeing the white horse still beneath the gallery, could not help calling, “Masters, are you still asleep?” “They are up,” said Sha Monk. He opened the door and let the princes in. When they saw no weapons, they asked in a fluster, “Have you put all your weapons away, Masters?” Monkey sprang up. “We certainly did not!” “All three weapons disappeared last night,” said the princes. Pigsy scrambled hastily to his feet. “Is my rake there?” The young princes said, “When we came out just now, everyone was searching high and low without finding them. Your disciples feared that our masters had put them away, so we came to ask. Your treasures can grow or shrink at will; surely you have hidden them on your persons to tease your disciples.” “We truly did not put them away,” said Monkey. Let us all go and search.”

p.src: They went together to the awning in the courtyard and, sure enough, found not a trace of the weapons. Pigsy said, “These blacksmiths must have stolen them. Hand them over at once! Delay another moment and I will beat every one of you to death—to death!” Terrified, the blacksmiths kowtowed with tears streaming down their faces. “Grandfather, we were exhausted from working for days and fell asleep last night. When we rose at dawn, the weapons were gone. We are mere mortals—how could we possibly lift them? We beg you, Grandfather, spare our lives! Spare us!” Monkey said nothing, but inwardly reproached himself: “This was our own fault. Once we had inspected the patterns, we should have kept the weapons by our sides. Why did we leave them lying here? Those treasures glowed with radiant light. They must have attracted some villain, who stole them under cover of night.” Pigsy did not believe him. “What are you saying, Brother? This is such a peaceful land, not some desolate wilderness or remote mountain. How could any villain come here? The blacksmiths must have acted treacherously. They saw the brilliance of our weapons and knew they were treasures, so during the night they slipped out of the prince’s residence, gathered accomplices, and had some carry and others drag them away. Bring them here and beat them! Beat them!” The craftsmen could only kowtow and swear their innocence.

p.src: Amid the uproar, the old prince appeared. When he learned what had happened, the color drained from his face. After pondering for a long while, he said, “The divine masters’ weapons are no ordinary things; even a hundred men together could not budge them. Moreover, my house has ruled this city for five generations. This is no empty boast, but I enjoy a modest reputation for virtue beyond its walls; and the soldiers, citizens, artisans, and workers of this city stand in considerable awe of my laws. They would certainly never dare to act treacherously. I beg the divine masters to reconsider.” Monkey laughed. “There is no need to reconsider, nor any need to keep blaming the blacksmiths. Let me ask Your Highness: are there any mountain or forest demons around this city?” The prince replied, “Divine Master, there is much sense in your question. North of my city stands Leopard-Head Mountain, and on that mountain there is a cave called Tiger’s Mouth. People often say that immortals live inside; others say there are tigers and wolves, and still others say there are demons. I have never discovered the truth and do not know what is actually there.” Monkey laughed. “Say no more. The villains there must have known the weapons were treasures and stolen them away in the night.” He called, “Pigsy, Sha Monk, stay here to protect Master and guard the city while I, Old Monkey, go and investigate.” He also ordered the blacksmiths not to let their forge fires go out, but to continue making every piece.

p.src: As Monkey was looking about, he suddenly heard voices behind the mountain. He turned quickly and saw two wolf-headed demons talking loudly as they walked northwest. Monkey surmised, “These must be monsters patrolling the mountain. I will follow and listen to what they are saying.” He formed a hand seal, recited a spell, shook himself, and changed into a little butterfly. Spreading his wings, he fluttered lightly after them. And a most convincing butterfly he became:

p.src: He fluttered above one demon’s head, drifting with the air as he listened to their conversation. One demon suddenly cried, “Second Brother, our king has enjoyed wonderful luck these past few days. Last month he obtained a beautiful woman and has been amusing himself with her in the cave, perfectly delighted; and last night he acquired three weapons as well, which truly are priceless treasures. Tomorrow he is giving a feast to celebrate the Rake, and we shall all share in the enjoyment.” The other replied, “We have had some luck too. We have these twenty taels of silver to buy pigs and sheep. When we reach the market at Qianfang, let us first drink a few pots of wine. Then we can pad the account for the purchases, skim off two or three taels, and buy ourselves padded coats for the winter. Would that not be fine?” Laughing and chatting, the two demons took to the main road and sped along as though flying.

p.src: When Monkey heard about the feast celebrating the rake, he rejoiced inwardly. He wanted to kill the pair, but they were not responsible for the theft, and besides, he had no weapon in his hand. He flew ahead, resumed his true form, and planted himself at a crossroads. As the demons drew near, he spat a mouthful of magic spittle at them and uttered, “Om hum zha li!” Then he cast an immobilizing spell and froze both wolf-headed fiends in place. Their eyes stared wide, but their mouths could not open; their bodies stood rigid, both feet fixed to the ground. Monkey then toppled them over, opened their clothes, and searched them. Sure enough, he found twenty taels of silver in a pouch fastened to the sash at their waists; each also wore a white-painted tablet. One was inscribed “Crafty Freak,” and the other “Freakish Craft.”

p.src: The Great Sage took their silver, removed their tablets, and hurried back to the city. At the prince’s residence he met the prince, the Tang Monk, the officials high and low, and all the craftsmen, and related everything that had happened. Pigsy laughed. “It must be because my treasure shines with such radiant splendor that they are buying pigs and sheep and preparing a feast to celebrate it. But how are we to recover it now?” Monkey said, “All three of us brothers shall go. This silver was meant for buying pigs and sheep. For now, give it as a reward to the craftsmen, and have His Highness procure several pigs and sheep. Pigsy, you change into Crafty Freak, and I shall become Freakish Craft. Sha Monk will pose as a livestock dealer selling pigs and sheep. We shall enter Tiger’s Mouth Cave and, when the chance comes, each seize our weapon, wipe out those fiends, then return and prepare to resume our journey.” Sha Monk laughed. “Splendid, splendid, splendid! We must not delay. Let us go at once.” The old prince followed the plan exactly, ordering his steward to procure seven or eight pigs and four or five whole sheep.

p.src: The three disciples took leave of their master and displayed their magic powers outside the city. Bajie said, “Brother, I never saw that Crafty Devil. How am I to change into his likeness?” Wukong said, “That fiend is still standing where I froze him with my body-fixing spell, and he will not awaken until this time tomorrow. I remember what he looks like. Stand still and let me teach you how to transform. …Thus and so—and there you have his likeness.” The fool duly recited the spell, and Wukong blew a breath of immortal air over him. In an instant he became the exact image of Crafty Devil, with a white tally hanging at his waist. Wukong himself changed into Devilish Craft and also hung a tally at his waist. Sha Wujing disguised himself as a livestock dealer who traded in pigs and sheep. Together they drove the pigs and sheep onto the highway and headed straight for the mountain.

p.src: The fiend carried a brightly lacquered invitation case under his left arm. Coming up to Wukong, he called, “Devilish Craft and Crafty Devil, so you two are back? How many pigs and sheep did you buy?” Wukong replied, “Aren’t these the ones we are driving?” The fiend gestured toward Sha Wujing and asked, “Who is this fellow?” Wukong said, “He is the dealer who sold us the pigs and sheep. We still owe him a few taels of silver, so we brought him home to collect it. Where are you going?” The fiend replied, “I am going to Bamboo-Joint Mountain to invite the Senior King to tomorrow morning’s banquet.” Adopting the fiend’s familiar tone, Wukong asked, “How many guests are being invited altogether?” The fiend replied, “The Senior King will occupy the seat of honor. Together with our mountain’s king, the chiefs, and the rest, there will be more than forty guests.” As they spoke, Bajie said, “Let’s go, let’s go! The pigs and sheep are scattering everywhere.” Wukong said, “Go round them up while I ask to see his invitation.” Taking him for one of their own, the fiend opened the case, drew out the invitation, and handed it to Wukong. p.src: Sha Wujing asked, “Brother, what did the invitation say?” Wukong replied, “It was an invitation to a celebration in honor of the rake. It was signed, ‘Your disciple, Yellow Lion, bows his head and pays a hundred obeisances.’ The guest invited was their revered ancestor, the venerable Nine-Spirit Sage.” Sha Wujing laughed and said, “Yellow Lion must surely be a golden-maned lion that has become a spirit. But what sort of creature is this Nine-Spirit Sage?” Hearing this, Bajie laughed and said, “He is prey fit for Old Hog.” Wukong asked, “What makes you think he is your prey?” Bajie replied, “The ancients said, ‘A mangy sow always chases golden-maned lions.’ That is how I know he belongs to Old Hog.” Talking and laughing, the three drove the pigs and sheep onward until the entrance to Tiger-Mouth Cave came into view. Outside the entrance they saw:

p.src: As they gradually approached the entrance, they saw a motley crowd of fiends, large and small, playing beneath the flowering trees. When they heard Bajie shouting “Ho! Ho!” as he drove up the pigs and sheep, they all came to meet them. Some seized the pigs, others the sheep, and together they bound every animal. The commotion soon alerted the fiend king inside. Leading more than ten little fiends out, he asked, “So you two are back? How many pigs and sheep did you buy?” Wukong replied, “We bought eight pigs and seven dressed sheep, fifteen head of livestock altogether. The pigs cost sixteen taels of silver and the sheep nine. We were given twenty taels before, so five are still owing. This is the dealer, who has followed us here to collect the balance.” On hearing this, the fiend king called, “You little ones, fetch five taels of silver and send him on his way.” Wukong said, “The dealer came partly to collect his silver and partly to see the splendid celebration.” The fiend flew into a rage and cursed, “You wretched Crafty Devil! Buying the goods was enough. Why did you go telling an outsider anything about our celebration?” Bajie stepped forward and said, “Our lord has obtained a treasure that truly is a marvel without equal beneath Heaven. What harm can there be in letting him look at it?” The fiend barked, “You hateful Devilish Craft! I obtained this treasure in the city of Yuhua Prefecture. If this dealer sees it and spreads word of it there, what shall we do if the princes suddenly come seeking it?” Wukong said, “My lord, this dealer lives beyond Qianfang Market, a great distance from the prefecture, and is not a man of that city. How could he spread word there? Besides, he is hungry, and neither of us has eaten. Since food and wine are ready in the house, give him some, then send him away.” Before he had finished speaking, a little fiend brought five taels of silver and handed them to Wukong. Wukong passed the silver to Sha Wujing and said, “Dealer, take your silver. Come with us to the rear and have something to eat.”

p.src: Mustering his courage, Sha Wujing entered the cave with Bajie and Wukong. When they reached the hall in the second courtyard, they saw a nine-pronged rake enshrined high upon the table in the center, shining so brilliantly that it dazzled the eyes. A gold-banded cudgel leaned against the eastern wall, and a demon-quelling staff against the western wall. The fiend king followed them in and said, “Dealer, that shining object in the middle is the rake. You may look at it, but once you leave, you must tell no one.” Sha Wujing nodded and thanked him.

p.src: Ah! As the saying goes: When a thing sees its master, it is certain to be reclaimed. Bajie had always been a rough and reckless fellow. The instant he saw his rake, he had no patience for any further pretense. He rushed forward, snatched it down, whirled it in his hands, resumed his true form, brandished the weapon, and raked straight at the fiend’s face. Wukong and Sha Wujing also dashed to the two sides, each seized his weapon and resumed his true form, and the three brothers attacked together in a wild melee. The fiend king, terrified, hastily twisted aside and dodged. Retreating to the rear, he fetched a four-bladed spade with a long shaft and sharp metal butt, then rushed into the courtyard and parried all three weapons. He shouted fiercely, “Who are you, to dare play tricks and cheat me of my treasures?” Wukong cursed, “You thieving ball of fur! You do not recognize me. We are disciples of the holy monk Tang Sanzang from the Land of the East. When we reached Yuhua Prefecture to exchange our travel credentials, the worthy king had his three princes take us as masters and learn the martial arts, using our treasures as models for weapons of the same design. We left them in the courtyard, but you thieving furball slipped into the city by night and stole them. And now you accuse us of trickery and cheating you of your treasures! Do not run away! Let us treat you to a few strokes from each of our three weapons.” The fiend raised his spade and met their attack. The battle carried them from the courtyard out through the front gate. See how the three monks closed upon the single fiend—a splendid fight indeed:

p.src: They fought for a long while on Leopard-Head Mountain. Unable to withstand them, the fiend shouted at Sha Wujing, “Take my spade!” Sha Wujing twisted aside and dodged the blow. The fiend seized the opening to escape and flew away on the wind toward the southeast. Bajie lengthened his stride to pursue him, but Wukong said, “Let him go for now. As the old saying goes, ‘Do not pursue a desperate foe.’ Let us first cut off his route home.” Bajie did as he was told.

Bajie lengthened his stride to pursue him, but Wukong said, “Let him go for now.
As the old saying goes, ‘Do not pursue a desperate foe.’
Let us first cut off his route home.”
Bajie did as he was told.

p.src: The three went straight to the cave entrance and killed every one of the hundred-odd demons, great and small. They proved to be tigers, wolves, striped leopards, panthers, horses, deer, and goats. The Great Sage then worked a spell and had all the valuables in the cave, the bodies of the various slain beasts, and the pigs and sheep that had been driven there carried outside. Sha Monk brought out dry firewood and set it alight, while Eight Rules fanned the flames with his two ears; in no time they burned the lair utterly clean. Taking everything they had brought out, they then returned at once to the prefectural city.

p.src: At this time the city gates were still open and the townspeople had not yet gone to sleep. The old king, his sons, and the Tang monk were all waiting in the gauze pavilion when they saw the three return and, with a great clatter, throw down a courtyardful of dead beasts, pigs, sheep, and valuables. Together they cried, “Master, we have returned victorious!” The princes repeatedly expressed their thanks. The elder of Tang was delighted. The three young princes knelt and bowed, but Sha Monk helped them up, saying, “Do not thank us yet. Come closer and look at these things.” The princes asked, “Where did all these things come from?” Pilgrim laughed. “Those tigers, wolves, striped leopards, panthers, horses, deer, and goats were all beasts that had become demons. After recovering our weapons, we fought our way out through the gate. The old demon was a golden-maned lion. Wielding a four-bladed spade, he fought us until nightfall, then fled defeated toward the southeast. We did not pursue him. Instead, we swept away the refuge to which he might return, killed this host of demons, searched out these possessions of his, and brought them here.” Hearing this, the old king was both happy and worried: happy that they had returned victorious, but worried that the demon would later seek revenge. Pilgrim said, “Set your mind at ease, Your Highness. I have considered the matter thoroughly and know how to deal with it. We shall not depart until we have swept them away root and branch; we certainly will not leave behind trouble for the future. When I went out at noon, I met a little blue-faced, red-haired demon delivering an invitation. On his card I read: ‘Tomorrow morning, with due respect, a banquet of food and wine will be prepared to celebrate the splendid Rake Gathering. We humbly beg you to honor us by crossing the mountain for a visit. Pray do not regard yourself as an outsider; we shall be most grateful. Respectfully presented to our honored grandsire, the Great Sage Nine-Spirit.’ It was signed, ‘Your disciple and grandson Yellow Lion, with a hundred prostrations.’ Now that the demon has been defeated, he must have gone to confer with his grandsire. Tomorrow morning they will certainly come seeking revenge upon us, so it is only right that we wipe them out completely for you.” The old king thanked him and ordered the evening vegetarian meal to be served. When master and disciples had finished their meal, each retired to his sleeping quarters. Of this we shall speak no more.

p.src: Now the demon did indeed flee southeastward to Bamboo Joint Mountain. Within that mountain was a cave blessed by nature, called the Nine-Bend Winding Cave. The Great Sage Nine-Spirit who dwelt in the cave was his grandsire. He traveled all night without pausing and reached the cave entrance around the fifth watch, where he knocked and went inside. A little demon saw him and said, “Great King, Blue-Face brought your invitation last night. Our lord kept him here until this morning and was about to come with him to attend your Rake Gathering. Why have you come so very early to invite him in person?” The demon said, “It is a sorry tale—a sorry tale! The gathering cannot be held.” As he spoke, Blue-Face came out from within and said, “Great King, what brings you here? As soon as the Old Great King rises, he is coming with me to attend the gathering.” The demon, flustered and distressed, merely waved his hands without speaking.

p.src: Presently the old demon arose and summoned him inside. The demon cast aside his weapon, prostrated himself, and could not keep the tears from streaming down his cheeks. The old demon said, “Worthy grandson, yesterday you sent an invitation, and this morning I was just about to attend your gathering. Why have you come in person, weeping and distressed?” The demon kowtowed and said, “The night before last, your little grandson was strolling idly beneath the moon when I saw a radiance soaring into the sky from the city of Jade-Flower Prefecture. I hurried over to look and found that three weapons in the royal residence were emitting the light: a nine-toothed gold-inlaid rake, a precious staff, and a gold-hooped cudgel. I immediately used my magic to draw them to me and named the celebration the ‘Splendid Rake Gathering.’ I ordered my underlings to buy pigs, sheep, fruit, and other provisions and prepare a feast, intending to invite Grandfather to admire the weapons and share the pleasure. Yesterday, after I sent Blue-Face to deliver the invitation, Diaozuan and the others, whom I had sent to buy pigs and sheep, came driving several animals and brought with them a merchant demanding his silver. He insisted on seeing the gathering, but I feared he would spread word of it outside and refused to let him look. Then he said he was hungry and asked for food, so I had him fed in the rear quarters. He went inside, saw the weapons, and declared that they belonged to him. The three men each seized one weapon and revealed their true forms: one was a monk with a hairy face and a Thunder Duke’s beak, one a monk with a long snout and huge ears, and one a monk with a dark, ill-favored face. Without asking who was right or wrong, they gave a shout and began striking wildly. I hastily took up my four-bladed spade, pursued them, and confronted them, demanding to know who they were and why they dared play such tricks. They said they were disciples of the Tang monk, who had been sent from the Great Tang in the Eastern Land to the Western Heaven. While passing through the prefectural city to exchange their travel rescript, they had been detained by the princes to teach them martial arts. These three weapons had been left in the courtyard as models for copies to be forged, and because I stole them, they angrily fought me. I do not know the names of those three monks, but all of them possess great abilities. I alone could not withstand all three, and so I fled here to Grandfather. I beg you to lend me your strength, capture those monks, and avenge me, thereby showing a grandfather’s love for his grandson.”

p.src: Hearing this, the old demon pondered silently for a moment, then laughed. “So it was he! Worthy grandson, you have provoked the wrong man.” The demon asked, “Grandfather, do you know who he is?” The old demon said, “The one with the long snout and huge ears is Zhu Eight Rules; the one with the dark, ill-favored face is Sha Monk. Those two are still manageable. The one with the hairy face and Thunder Duke’s beak is called Sun the Pilgrim. He possesses truly immense supernatural powers. Five hundred years ago he caused havoc in Heaven, and even a hundred thousand celestial soldiers could not capture him. He makes a particular business of hunting people down—a veritable chief constable of combing mountains, overturning seas, breaking caves, storming cities, and stirring up trouble. Why did you provoke him? No matter. I shall go with you, capture that fellow along with the princes of Jade-Flower, and let you vent your anger upon them.” Hearing this, the demon immediately kowtowed in thanks.

p.src: The old demon thereupon summoned his grandsons Tawny Lion, Snow Lion, Suanni, White Marsh, Crouching Lynx, and Elephant Catcher. Each took up a keen weapon, and with Yellow Lion leading them, they all rode wild winds directly to the borders of Leopard-Head Mountain. They caught the sharp smell of smoke and fire, and also heard the sound of weeping. Looking carefully, they saw that it was Diaozuan and Guguai, crying there and calling for their master. The demon approached and shouted, “Are you the real Diaozuan or a false one?” The two monsters fell to their knees and, with tears in their eyes, kowtowed and said, “How could we be false? About this time yesterday, we took the silver and went to buy pigs and sheep. When we reached the main road west of the mountain, we met a monk with a hairy face and a Thunder Duke’s beak. He spat at us, and at once our legs went weak, our mouths grew stiff, and we could neither speak nor move. He knocked us down, searched us, took the silver, and removed our identity tablets. The two of us remained dazed and unconscious until we finally awoke just now. When we reached home, the smoke and flames had not yet died away, and all the buildings had been burned down. Nor could we find our master or any of the leaders, great or small. That is why we are here weeping in grief. We do not know how this fire started.”

p.src: When the monster heard this, he could not hold back his tears, which gushed forth like a spring. Stamping both feet and shouting so loudly that the heavens rang, he cried bitterly, “You bald scoundrels! How could you commit such utter wickedness and do a thing so cruel? You burned my whole cave dwelling to ashes, burned my beauties to death, and wiped out my household, young and old, along with all my possessions. I shall die of rage! I shall die of rage!” The old monster ordered the Macaque Lion to pull him over and said, “Worthy grandson, now that matters have come to this, vexing yourself will do no good. Preserve your full strength for now, and then go into the prefectural city and seize that monk.” Still the monster would not stop weeping. “Grandfather,” he said, “that mountain domain of mine was not built in a day. Now that these bald scoundrels have destroyed it all, what use have I for this life?” He struggled to his feet and tried to dash his head against the rocky cliff. Only after the Snow Lion, the Macaque Lion, and the others earnestly restrained and consoled him did he desist.

p.src: They then abandoned that place and all made for the prefectural city. Soon there came the sound of rolling wind and billowing mist, drawing very near. The people in every suburb beyond the city walls were so terrified that, dragging their sons and carrying their daughters, they abandoned their belongings and fled into the city. Once they had passed through the gates, the gates were shut. Someone hurried into the royal residence to report, “Disaster! Disaster!” The prince, Tripitaka, and the others were taking their morning vegetarian meal in the Baosha Pavilion. Hearing the report of disaster, they came out to inquire what had happened. The people said, “A band of monsters is nearing the city, sending sand and stones flying, spewing mist, and whipping up the wind.” The old king was greatly alarmed. “What are we to do?” he asked. Monkey laughed. “Set your minds at ease, all of you. Set your minds at ease. The monsters of Tiger’s Mouth Cave were defeated yesterday, and they have gone southeast to enlist that Nine-Spirits Primal Sage or whatever he is called. Let me and my brothers go out to meet them. Give orders to close all four gates, and muster men to guard the city walls.” The prince accordingly issued orders to close the four gates and mustered men atop the walls. He and his father, together with Tripitaka, directed the defenses from the gate tower, while banners blotted out the sun and cannon fire thundered without cease. Monkey and his two companions, half riding cloud and half shrouded in mist, went out of the city to meet the enemy. Indeed:
